newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rules out renegotiating 1996 economic pact.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rules out renegotiating 1996 economic pact.

text.p: The Mexican government on Thursday ruled out renegotiating the current economic pact signed with business and labor, according to the official news agency Notimex, which quoted Labour Secretary Javier Bonilla.
The wide-ranging annual pact, which sets macroeconomic targets and guidelines for wage and price rises, was completed at the end of October 1995 and is valid until the end of 1996.
Labour unions have suggested the last increase in the minimum wage -- a 10 percent rise in April -- was insufficient and the agreement needed revision before the end of the year.
Business leaders and the government are opposed to any interim wage increase.

Notimex quoted Bonilla as saying the current pact was valid until December 31. He said the union leaders who had called for a wage rise were isolated voices who were not representative of the labour movement as a whole, according to the agency.
